stage0_classify.classification_rationale: The startup addresses a real, urgent, structural problem in Peruvian healthcare administration: manual medical authorization processing is slow and costly. Large insurers (Rimac, Pacifico, Sanitas) have clear budgets and incentives to reduce costs, making them willing buyers. Outcome-based pricing aligns with their interests, and the AI solution offers a significant improvement over current manual workflows.
stage0_classify.freemium_rationale: Freemium is not suitable for this B2B enterprise sale. The product is outcome-based per authorization, and the target buyers (large insurers) require custom demonstrations and proof of value before purchasing. A free tier would not attract these buyers and could dilute the perceived value.
stage0_classify.payment_blocker: EPS procurement teams may resist outcome-based billing due to budgeting unpredictability and require fixed monthly fees; furthermore, measuring 'authorizations processed' accurately without manual verification is contentious.
stage0_classify.free_substitute_risk: The current manual process (human auditors) is the default 'free' substitute; EPS can also invest in minor workflow improvements or hire more staff without switching to AI.
stage0_classify.market_size_reality_check: Peruvian EPS market is small (3-5 major players); at ~$1/auth with thousands of auths/month per EPS, SAM in Peru is <$5M ARR. Must expand to Colombia/Mexico where competition and localization costs are higher.
stage0_classify.hardest_assumption: That EPS will trust an external AI for a core, liability-sensitive medical decision process without extensive validation and contractual indemnification.
stage0_classify.devil_rationale: While the idea addresses a real pain point, the combination of long enterprise sales cycles, regulatory/liability risks, and small addressable market in Peru makes it a weak bet for venture scale. Success hinges on rapid expansion to larger LATAM markets and overcoming deep trust barriers, which is highly uncertain.

stage1_research.research_summary: The prior authorization automation market in Latin America is in its infancy, with no clear leader. The primary alternative remains manual review, which is slow and costly. Global AI players like Cohere Health and Olive show interest in the region, while BPOs like Sutherland leverage existing relationships. Internal EPS initiatives pose a threat if they succeed. The startup's main advantage is its outcome-based pricing and local focus, but speed to market is critical as competitors loom.

competitor_signals.sourcing_brief: Cohere Health has strong momentum in the US prior auth space with significant funding and marquee clients. Their announced LatAm pilot signals imminent expansion, making them the most dangerous potential entrant.
Sutherland's deep penetration in LatAm health payer operations gives them a distribution advantage, but their AI capabilities are not leading-edge, relying on partnerships.

Incumbent EPS IT teams are exploring RPA for prior auth, but lack AI expertise and face internal resistance. Their solutions are unlikely to match dedicated AI, but could delay adoption of external tools.

AuthFast is the only known direct AI competitor in the region, with a small but growing presence. Their local focus gives them cultural and regulatory advantages, but their scale and funding are limited.
Manual audit teams are the entrenched incumbent, with high switching costs for EPS but extreme inefficiency. They lack innovation capacity but benefit from organizational inertia.

gaps.title: Performance-Based Pricing with ROI Transparency
gaps.pain: High – Insurers face fixed costs with manual staff or BPOs regardless of volume, and are skeptical of AI's ROI. Per-authorization pricing aligns cost with value.
gaps.why_now: EPSs are under pressure to cut administrative costs (up to 30% of premiums) and want variable cost structures. No current solution offers pure outcome-based pricing in LATAM.
gaps.evidence_needed: Willingness-to-pay surveys from 5 EPS CFOs for a per-auth model; cost benchmarking of manual vs AI; a pilot that demonstrates cost savings.
gaps.risk: Pricing can be copied, but bundling with locally trained AI creates a temporary moat; some insurers may prefer annual licensing.

gaps.title: Seamless Integration with Legacy Systems
gaps.pain: High – EPSs run on aging IT infrastructures, making heavy integrations a multi-year project that stalls automation. A lightweight API-first approach can bypass this bottleneck.
gaps.why_now: AuthFast and global players often require deep integration; internal initiatives are slow. A plug-and-play solution can demonstrate value in weeks, not months.
gaps.evidence_needed: Technical feasibility study with 2–3 common EPS claim platforms; prototype integration that processes mock requests in real-time from a test EHR.
gaps.risk: Legacy system idiosyncrasies may still require custom work; large incumbents with consulting arms (Accenture) could replicate the integration layer eventually.

gaps.title: Explainable & Auditable AI Decisions
gaps.pain: High – Insurers face medico-legal risks if they deny care without clear justification. Existing AI tools often lack transparency, making them unsafe for Peruvian regulators.
gaps.why_now: Regulators (MINSA) increasingly demand documented reasoning for prior auth decisions. A solution that automatically generates evidence-backed audit trails can reduce liability and speed adoption.
gaps.evidence_needed: Review of regulatory requirements for authorization justifications; comparative analysis of explainability features in competitor tools; mock audit trail demonstration to legal teams.
gaps.risk: Building a comprehensive clinical knowledge graph is resource-intensive; over-explaining could clutter communication; competitors can add explainability layers.

gaps.title: Ultra-Fast Authorization for Patient Satisfaction
gaps.pain: Medium-High – Long waits (days) cause patient suffering and drop-off in care. Instant decisions could be a major differentiator for insurer NPS.
gaps.why_now: Telehealth growth increases demand for quick auth; competitors' speeds vary, but none guarantee <5 minutes end-to-end in the Peruvian context.
gaps.evidence_needed: Time-motion study of current manual process; benchmark of AI vs manual on latency; pilot with a small insurer measuring patient satisfaction improvements.
gaps.risk: Speed alone may not justify switching if accuracy is compromised; better integration can also reduce time.

gaps.title: Continuous Learning from Peruvian Data
gaps.pain: Medium – Initial AI accuracy may be lower without local data, but a model that improves over time will widen the moat.
gaps.why_now: Data is siloed in each EPS. A shared learning model (federated) or even single-insurer adaptation can create a self-reinforcing advantage.
gaps.evidence_needed: Data-sharing agreements to test model improvement over 6 months; technical plan for privacy-preserving fine-tuning; initial accuracy baseline.
gaps.risk: Requires sustained data access, which may be denied by insurers; competitors could negotiate for similar data.

gaps.title: Hybrid Human-AI Escalation for Complex Cases
gaps.pain: Medium – High-risk or rare cases still need human judgment, but routing them intelligently reduces cost while maintaining quality.
gaps.why_now: Pure AI solutions may over-automate and cause costly errors. A hybrid model that combines AI for routine approvals and escalates nuanced cases to a physician network can optimize both accuracy and cost.
gaps.evidence_needed: Analysis of what percentage of cases are truly complex; mock pilot with AI recommending escalation; partnership interest from on-call physician services.
gaps.risk: Human element reintroduces cost and slower turnaround; managing physician network is operationally complex.

iterations.idea_refined: EPS Admin AI automatiza el proceso de autorizaciones médicas en las EPS peruanas, comenzando por Rimac, Pacifico y Sanitas. Nuestra IA lee la solicitud del médico tratante, extrae el historial del afiliado de los sistemas legacy, interpreta las guías clínicas locales (que son distintas a las de otros países) y emite una recomendación inmediata de aprobación o rechazo con justificación explicable. Los auditores humanos solo intervienen en el 5-10% de casos que la IA marca como dudosos, eliminando horas de revisión manual y reduciendo el tiempo de respuesta de 30-120 minutos a segundos. El modelo de negocio es puro: cobramos por cada autorización procesada, alineando incentivos y demostrando ROI inmediato. Empezamos con procedimientos de alta complejidad (como cirugías y medicamentos oncológicos) donde el costo del error y la demora es más crítico. La diferenciación local es clave: entrenamos el modelo con datos peruanos, adaptándonos al español médico local, a los códigos de diagnóstico peruanos y a las coberturas específicas de cada EPS, algo que los gigantes globales no ofrecen.
iterations.one_liner: Reemplazamos la revisión manual de autorizaciones médicas en EPS peruanas con IA que decide en segundos usando guías locales, y cobramos solo por resultado.
iterations.target_customer: Médico Auditor de EPS peruanas (específicamente en Rimac, Pacifico o Sanitas) que pasa 4-6 horas al día revisando manualmente solicitudes de autorización en múltiples sistemas.
iterations.core_problem: Cada autorización toma entre 30 y 120 minutos de lectura y análisis manual. El auditor debe entrar a 3-5 sistemas distintos (historial clínico, guías de la EPS, normativas) copiar y pegar información, interpretar guías ambiguas y tomar decisiones de alto impacto con información fragmentada. Esto genera un cuello de botella de 200-500 solicitudes diarias por EPS, retrasos que irritan a pacientes y médicos, y costos operativos innecesarios (un auditor gana S/ 5,000-8,000 mensuales por procesar ~20 casos/día). El error humano por fatiga o inconsistencia puede causar autorizaciones indebidas o rechazos que terminan en quejas y sobrecostos legales.
iterations.solution_hook: IA entrenada exclusivamente con datos médicos peruanos, capaz de leer las guías clínicas locales (ej. guías de práctica clínica del Minsa adaptadas por cada EPS) y operar dentro de los sistemas legacy sin reemplazarlos, mediante integraciones ligeras (APIs o automatización de interfaz).
iterations.why_this_angle: Al enfocar la propuesta en la profunda necesidad de localización peruana —no solo idioma sino procesos clínicos y regulatorios únicos— nos diferenciamos radicalmente de soluciones genéricas en inglés o portugués. Construimos un foso temprano que los competidores globales no pueden replicar sin invertir años en adaptación. El nicho permite validar rápido con un EPS, probar el outcome-based pricing y luego expandir con el mismo ADN a otros países andinos.

iterations.idea_refined: Instead of selling to EPS, we target large Peruvian employers who provide private health plans to their workforce. These employers currently bear the hidden costs of slow manual prior authorizations: employee frustration, delayed treatments, absenteeism, and lack of transparency. Our AI solution integrates with their existing health plan administration (TPA or self-insured setup) to instantly process pre-authorizations using Peruvian clinical guidelines and employee history, delivering approvals or denials with explanations in seconds. The employer pays an annual per-employee fee, gaining a dashboard with ROI tracking, cost savings, and employee satisfaction metrics. Only edge cases are escalated to human auditors. This shifts the buyer from health insurance companies to HR departments managing benefits, aligning with their urgency to improve employee wellness and control escalating healthcare costs while offering a localized, transparent alternative to manual processes.
iterations.one_liner: We help large employers in Peru slash prior authorization wait times from days to seconds using localized AI, charging per employee per year.
iterations.target_customer: HR Director or Benefits Manager of a Peruvian company with 5,000+ employees, e.g., a mining conglomerate, responsible for negotiating health insurance contracts and employee wellness.
iterations.core_problem: Every month, hundreds of employees face 2-5 day waits for routine pre-authorizations due to overwhelmed manual review teams at the EPS. This causes employee dissatisfaction, health deterioration, and indirect costs like absenteeism and turnover. The employer has no direct control and sees rising premiums without transparency into inefficiencies.
iterations.solution_hook: Unlike generic AI authorization tools designed for US/EU markets, ours is built specifically for the Peruvian medical context, understands local clinical guidelines and Spanish medical terminology, and offers a per-employee pricing with clear ROI dashboards, making it a plug-and-play employee benefit upgrade rather than IT software.
iterations.why_this_angle: Selling to employers taps a more immediate budget—employee benefits—with a clear pain point (employee complaints, cost overruns) and a shorter sales cycle than selling to entrenched EPS institutions. The performance-based pricing per employee de-risks the purchase and aligns incentives. This framing also opens a B2B2C channel through employer-provided health apps.

The AI instantly recommends approve/reject with a justified rationale, reducing manual review from hours to seconds. Human auditors only review 5% of cases flagged as ambiguous. We charge per authorization processed, eliminating upfront software costs and proving immediate ROI through reduced backlogs, faster patient treatment, and lower legal risk.

Audit doctors are burned out and error-prone under the pressure.
iterations.solution_hook: Unlike generic AI tools, our model is fine-tuned on Rimac's proprietary oncology protocols and Peruvian drug regulations, making its decisions immediately auditable and compliant. The outcome-based pricing (pay only per processed authorization) removes financial risk and aligns with their operational budget.
iterations.why_this_angle: By hyper-focusing on one EPS and one critical specialty where pain is most acute (life-threatening delays), we can validate willingness to pay in 30 days with a pilot involving just 10 audit doctors. The narrow wedge demonstrates deep localization, builds trust through auditable decisions, and offers an ROI that is impossible to ignore, paving the way for expansion to other specialties and EPS.
